name: La Rochelle
title: Ship Thickness Measurement La Rochelle | UTM at La Pallice
description: Ultrasonic thickness gauging at La Rochelle-La Pallice for grain carriers, product tankers, timber ships and coasters: hull, tank and hatch coaming UTM.
h1: Ultrasonic Hull Gauging in La Rochelle and La Pallice
intro: La Rochelle's commercial harbour is La Pallice, a deep-water port on the Pertuis d'Antioche that loads cereals, takes in timber and forest products and handles oil products and bulk cargoes. Owners and superintendents ask for gauging here when a grain carrier or bulker has an intermediate or renewal survey coming, or when a charterer wants steel readings before a long laden passage. The inspection team travels from India to the ship for each job, so nothing is held in readiness on the Atlantic coast.
keywords: bulk carrier hull gauging la rochelle

highlights.p: Bulk carriers come to La Pallice to load cereals, and the holds are cleaned and inspected before loading. That clean-hold window is when hold frames, hopper tanks and hatch coamings can be read and recorded for the next survey.

La Pallice sits in open deep water, so ships berth at the outer quays without tidal gates. Superintendents can plan gauging against a berth sequence instead of a tide table, which suits short loading calls.

General cargo ships and bulkers carrying timber, pulp and wood products call regularly. Their hatch covers, coamings and tween-deck steel take handling damage that is worth measuring while the holds are open.

port.h: La Rochelle and La Pallice: the port and its approaches
p: The city of La Rochelle holds three separate harbours. The old harbour in the centre and the Minimes marina are for yachts, fishing boats and excursion craft, and are of little interest to merchant-ship gauging. The commercial port is La Pallice, a few kilometres to the west, which was built in the nineteenth century as a deep-water outport and is run today by the Grand Port Maritime de La Rochelle. Ships reach it from the Atlantic through the Pertuis d'Antioche, the channel between the Île de Ré to the north and the Île d'Oléron to the south, and the approach is pilotage-assisted and well marked.

Traffic at La Pallice is dominated by bulk and breakbulk trades. Cereals from the Poitou and Charente farmland are loaded for export, and the port has long been one of the main French grain outlets on the Atlantic side. Imports include fertiliser, animal feed ingredients, timber, forest products and sugar, together with refined oil products received at the oil berths. A ro-ro quay serves vehicle and project cargo, and a limited number of cruise and offshore-support calls fill in the rest of the year. Most merchant ships are handysize and supramax bulkers, product tankers and general cargo ships.

Gauging fits around loading rhythm. Grain ships arrive in ballast or part ballast, so topside and hopper ballast tanks are accessible and the holds are empty and swept before loading. Product tankers call to discharge, with tanks gas-free only when the ship plans it. Weather on this coast is mostly manageable, but Atlantic swell and autumn and winter gales can delay pilots and berthing, so a plan for anchored or waiting ships allows slack. Tidal range is large enough that the outer harbour and the inner basins behave differently, and it is worth confirming which side of the port a ship will use before the team is booked.

facilities.h: Where ships can be gauged at La Rochelle
p: Most gauging at La Pallice happens alongside, at the bulk and general cargo quays of the outer port, during the cargo stop. The agent arranges access through the port's security gate, and the ship provides a gas-free certificate and an enclosed-space entry permit for every ballast tank or hold space the team enters. Because loading cycles for grain are short, the plan is tank-first: ballast tanks and cofferdams while the ship waits for cargo, hold structure and hatch coamings once the holds are swept and before loading begins.

The port has a ship-repair side that has worked on coasters, fishing vessels and smaller merchant ships, and a repair dock exists on the commercial side. Its availability and size should be confirmed with the port authority and the yard before a docking-linked job is built around it. Larger ships that need a docking in dry dock normally go to a bigger Atlantic or Mediterranean yard, and in that case La Rochelle is the pre-docking call, where gauging readings help the yard scope steel renewal before the ship leaves.
list: Outer-port bulk quays at La Pallice, for hold, hopper tank and hatch coaming gauging on grain carriers.
Oil product berths, for ballast tank and deck gauging on product tankers within terminal permit rules.
General cargo and timber quays, for hatch cover, tween-deck and coaming steel on breakbulk ships.
Ro-ro quay, for ramp, vehicle deck and ballast tank checks on short calls.
The commercial port's repair dock and repair quay, for smaller ships and workboats, subject to availability.
Waiting berths in the outer harbour and the Pertuis d'Antioche anchorage, for launch-served work in settled weather.

context.h: Port state control and the grain trade at La Rochelle
p: France inspects foreign ships under the Paris MoU, through the Centres de sécurité des navires, which are the maritime administration's ship safety centres. Ships calling at La Pallice are targeted like those at any French port, with older bulkers and general cargo ships on the higher-risk list more likely to see a detailed inspection. A recent steel gauging report on the hull and hold structure is a useful piece of evidence for a master who expects an inspector on board.

Bulk carriers carry the strongest survey obligations here. The enhanced survey programme sets the extent of gauging at renewal surveys for bulk carriers, and charterers loading grain often ask owners to confirm hold condition. The EU Ship Recycling Regulation also expects an inventory of hazardous materials on board ships calling at EU ports, which is a separate paper task, but the same dry dock or repair programme usually serves both. EU ETS and FuelEU Maritime apply to calls at La Rochelle in the same way as at any other EU port.

jobs.h: Typical gauging jobs at La Pallice
jobs.p: Work at La Rochelle follows the grain and timber trades. Planning starts from the loading programme, the ship's survey due dates and whether a docking is already fixed elsewhere. Ultrasonic thickness measurement here usually covers:
list: Hold frame, hopper and topside tank gauging on a supramax bulker, taken after hold cleaning and before grain loading.
Hatch cover panel and coaming gauging on a timber carrier whose covers have taken crane and lashing damage.
Ballast tank and cofferdam gauging on a product tanker discharging at the oil berth, ahead of a vetting inspection.
Pre-docking steel estimate on a coaster heading for dry dock, with readings agreed with the superintendent and the yard.
Owner's condition gauging on a general cargo ship before a time charter, covering deck, bulwark and ballast tank steel.

logistics: Most technicians reach La Rochelle through Paris or Bordeaux, and La Rochelle-Île de Ré airport is a regional option when schedules allow. Roads connect the airports and the port, and the agent arranges gate passes and any launch for ships waiting outside. France is in the Schengen area, so each technician needs a Schengen visa issued in India before departure, which sets the lead time and is why a ship's loading date should be shared as early as possible.
vessels: General cargo ships and timber carriers

faqs.q: Can holds be gauged at La Pallice before grain is loaded?
faqs.a: Yes, that is the usual window. Once the holds are swept, washed and dry and the ship has a valid permit for entry, the team can read frames, hopper plating and coamings. Readings are recorded by location so the superintendent can see wasted areas before loading begins, and the report is ready for the next survey or for a charterer's request.

faqs.q: Is there a drydock at La Rochelle for steel renewal?
faqs.a: A repair dock exists on the commercial side, but its size and availability change, so it should be confirmed with the port authority and the yard. Large merchant ships usually dock at a bigger yard on the Atlantic or Mediterranean coast, and La Rochelle then serves as the pre-docking gauging stop that helps the yard scope steel work.

faqs.q: Can a ship be gauged at the Pertuis d'Antioche anchorage?
faqs.a: Sometimes. Ballast tanks and deck structure can be gauged at anchor in settled weather when launch transfers are safe. Swell or a strong onshore wind can cancel a transfer on short notice, so anchored work carries a weather allowance and a fallback alongside, which the agent agrees with the master and the pilots.

faqs.q: Do tidal conditions affect gauging at La Rochelle?
faqs.a: The outer berths at La Pallice are open to deep water, so tide does not limit berthing the way it does at lock-gated ports. It can matter for the inner basins and for deck access to the quay, so we check the berth and the expected freeboard before booking the team.

faqs.q: What documents does the ship need for tank entry at La Pallice?
faqs.a: A gas-free certificate and an enclosed-space entry permit for each tank or space, a rescue plan, and ventilation running throughout. Terminals may add their own permit when the ship is alongside during cargo work. The superintendent normally sends these to the agent and the team before arrival so the sequence of spaces is agreed in advance.
